summary: Sakkottai Krishnaswamy Aiyangar studied at the University of Madras (graduating in history by 1897, M.A. circa 1897-1899). He was a lecturer at Bangalore University (1899-1909) and held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914-1929).

Working in religious studies, Sakunoshin Motoda studied at Kenyon College (~1887-1891), the University of Pennsylvania (~1891-1895), and Columbia University. He later held a post at Rikkyo University (~1907-1923).
Sakutaro Fujioka worked in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1894 to 1897 and held a post there from circa 1900 to 1910.
A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Sakya Trizin founded Sakya College and taught Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche. He served as abbot at Sakya Monastery until 2017.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under teachers including Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, Khenpo Appey, and Chogye Trichen. He founded the Sakya Centre (1964), Sakya College, and Sakya Institute, and taught numerous students.

Active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, he studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, whom he succeeded. He served on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, Sallie B. King studied under Leon Hurvitz at the University of British Columbia (~1973-1975). She served as a professor and later Professor Emerita at James Madison University (~1992-2008).

An Indologist, Sally J. Sutherland Goldman earned her PhD at UC Berkeley (1979) and studied under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri. She held posts at UC Berkeley, where she is Senior Lecturer Emerita.
Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Sally McAra completed her MA at the University of Auckland (1999-2000), where she studied under supervisors Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.
Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, Sally Mellick Cutler earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1993. In 1997, she is attested as manager of the Pali Text Society Office.

An Indologist and linguist, Salomon Lefmann studied at Münster, Berlin (Ph.D. under Franz Bopp), Paris, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University starting in 1866, becoming associate professor in 1870 and honorary professor in 1901.

Working in Indology, history, and archaeology, Saloni Mathur holds posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, attested as Associate Professor of Art History in 2011 and as Department Chair and Professor of Modern & Contemporary South Asian Art in 2026.
Salvador E. Luria studied at Turin, Rome, and Columbia. He held posts at Columbia (~1940-1942), Indiana (1943), Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1950-1959), and MIT (~1959-1991).

Sam Harris studied philosophy at Stanford (1997-2000), earned a Ph.D. at UCLA (~2003-2009), and studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. His fields include philosophy and religious studies.

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under teachers including Lama Jampa Thaye and earned his PhD at Manchester (~1996-2000). He held posts at the British Library (from 1999) and SOAS University of London.
Active in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, Samani Pratibha Pragya earned a PhD at SOAS University of London and held a post there as a research assistant, attested in 2020.
Working in Indology, Sambhavi Ganesh is attested in 2026 as a doctoral student at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Radhika Govinda.

Working in Indology and religious studies, Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti held a post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1974 to 2005 and is attested in 2026 as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society.
Sampan Chakrabarty works in Indology. Attested in 2026, he studied for his doctorate under Pallab Sengupta and held a position as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

A Tibetology and religious studies scholar, he studied at Drepung Monastery and the University of London (PhD under David Snellgrove). He held posts at SOAS, Collège de France, and CNRS, and was President of the IATS (1995-2000).
